assumptions_made: The Hugging Face dataset was not suitable for the experiment's requirements, so we fell back to synthetic data generation
The synthetic dataset was designed to mimic the characteristics of the real dataset while ensuring proper imbalance (roughly 10% positive class)
The synthetic features were created with realistic correlations to ensure meaningful classification patterns
The experiment uses a fixed 75/25 train/test split with stratification to maintain class distribution
The logistic regression models are trained with sufficient iterations to converge
The evaluation metrics are calculated correctly according to standard definitions

results.hypothesis: Test whether class-weighted logistic regression improves minority-class recall over an unweighted baseline on imbalanced tabular data.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Unweighted logistic regression on the same split.
results.success_criteria: Weighted model improves minority-class recall by at least 0.05 without losing more than 0.03 accuracy.
results.notes: Weighted model did not improve minority-class recall by enough (0.010 < 0.05) but lost only -0.001 in accuracy.
results.methodological_validity: mixed real and synthetic inputs — findings are NOT interpretable as evidence; the synthetic inputs are listed in data_provenance.json
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
